title: FRANCE OPENS NUCLEAR DETERRENCE TO EUROPE IN HISTORIC COLD WAR-SCALE REALIGNMENT
excerpt: France initiates a historic shift in nuclear doctrine, opening deterrence capabilities to European allies. Germany commits to Europe's strongest conventional army amid a Franco-German security pivot.
body: France has initiated a historic shift in its nuclear doctrine, opening its deterrence capabilities to European allies in what President Macron calls 'forward deterrence' (dissuasion avancÃ©e). This marks a significant departure from decades of Gaullist nuclear sovereignty. Germany, under Chancellor Merz, has committed to building Europe's strongest conventional army, including a permanent brigade deployment to Lithuania. The Franco-German axis is forming the backbone of a new European security architecture as NATO faces an uncertain future. Key developments include joint nuclear steering groups, Baltic Brigade deployment, and responses to perceived US unreliability.
